quote: `match` is now a reserved keyword.
reason: A function called match is the existing syntax.reserved_name (ReservedNames); a class, interface or trait called match (a parse error from 8.0, in a namespace too) is the new syntax.match_class_name (Php80BicCoreMatchClassName); methods and class constants called match still work on 8.0 and are not reported.

quote: Assertion failures now throw by default.
reason: Whether an assert() fails depends on the value it checks (and on zend.assertions); the runtimes show a warning on 7.4 and an uncaught AssertionError from 8.0.

quote: Methods with the same name as the class are no longer interpreted as constructors.
reason: Covered by the existing OldConstructor rule and its fixtures.

quote: Removed ability to call non-static methods statically.
reason: Php80BicCoreNonStaticCall reports Class::method(), call_user_func( array( 'Class', 'method' ) ) / 'Class::method' (deprecated 7.0, Error from 8.0) and is_callable() of such a callable (true on 7.4, false from 8.0), only when class and method are in the same file and the call cannot have a $this of that class; calls in closures and through WordPress hooks (add_action) are not judged.

quote: Removed (real) cast.
reason: Covered by the existing Casts rule.

quote: Removed (unset) cast.
reason: Covered by the existing Casts rule.

quote: Removed track_errors ini directive.
reason: Php80BicCorePhpErrormsg reports a read of $php_errormsg after an @ in the same scope (changed in 8.0: it is never set); the runtimes show no deprecation on 7.4 for ini_set( 'track_errors' ), and from 8.0 ini_set/ini_get of it return false.

quote: Removed the ability to define case-insensitive constants.
reason: Php80BicCoreDefineCaseInsensitive reports define( 'NAME', v, true ) when the same file uses the constant in another case (unqualified or \NAME; Other\NAME is another constant) (deprecated 7.3, Error from 8.0); with every use in the defined case the runtimes show only a warning from 8.0 and the same output, which no finding level describes, so that part is not reported.

quote: Access to undefined constants now always results in an Error exception.
reason: Whether a bare constant is defined depends on what other files (WordPress core, other plugins) define at run time; 7.4 warned and used the name as a string, 8.0 throws Error.

quote: Removed ability to specify an autoloader using an __autoload() function.
reason: Php80BicCoreAutoloadFunction reports a global function named __autoload (deprecated 7.2 at compile time, a compile error from 8.0 even if never used); namespaced functions and methods of that name are fine on 8.0.

quote: Removed the $errcontext argument for custom error handlers.
reason: Php80BicCoreErrorHandlerContext reports a set_error_handler() closure, arrow function or same-file function whose fifth parameter has no default: ArgumentCountError from 8.0 at the first error; 7.4 raised no deprecation for it.

quote: Removed create_function().
reason: create_function is in data/catalog/functions.php (deprecated 7.2, removed 8.0) and reported by InternalFunctions.

quote: Removed each().
reason: each is in data/catalog/functions.php (deprecated 7.2, removed 8.0) and reported by InternalFunctions.

quote: Removed ability to unbind $this from closures that were created from a method, using Closure::fromCallable() or ReflectionMethod::getClosure().
reason: Depends on which closure object reaches bindTo( null ) at run time; the runtimes show a deprecation and an unbound closure on 7.4, a warning and null from 8.0.

quote: Also removed ability to unbind $this from proper closures that contain uses of $this.
reason: Depends on which closure reaches bindTo( null ) at run time; deprecated on 7.4, a warning and null from 8.0.

quote: Removed ability to use array_key_exists() with objects.
reason: Whether the second argument is an object is a run-time value; deprecated on 7.4, TypeError from 8.0.

quote: Made the behavior of array_key_exists() regarding the type of the key parameter consistent with isset() and normal array access.
reason: Depends on the type of the key value; a bool key gave a warning and false on 7.4 and is coerced (true) from 8.0.

quote: Any array that has a number n as its first numeric key will use n+1 for its next implicit key, even if n is negative.
reason: Php80BicCoreNegativeArrayKey works out the keys of an array literal with literal keys on both versions and reports it when they differ (changed in 8.0, also with variable values); appending to an existing array ($a[] = after $a[-5]) changed only in 8.3 on the runtimes and belongs to the 8.3 ledger.

quote: The default error_reporting level is now E_ALL.
reason: A php.ini default (error_reporting), not something PHP source code expresses.

quote: display_startup_errors is now enabled by default.
reason: A php.ini default (display_startup_errors), not something PHP source code expresses.

quote: Using "parent" inside a class that has no parent will now result in a fatal compile-time error.
reason: Php80BicCoreParentWithoutParent reports parent (calls, constants, new parent, types) in a class or anonymous class without extends: deprecated 7.4 at compile time, compile error from 8.0; inside closures the runtimes compile it on 8.0, so those are not reported.

quote: The @ operator will no longer silence fatal errors (E_ERROR, E_CORE_ERROR, E_COMPILE_ERROR, E_USER_ERROR, E_RECOVERABLE_ERROR, E_PARSE).
reason: Php80BicCoreErrorReportingZero reports error_reporting() == / === / != / !== 0 and ! error_reporting() inside a function, method or closure with two to five parameters in a file that calls set_error_handler (the handler idiom the notes name; elsewhere the comparison asks whether reporting is off altogether, which means the same on 8.0): on @ the handler saw 0 on 7.4 and 4437 from 8.0 (changed). That @ no longer hides fatal errors themselves depends on run time and is not reported.

quote: Following the hash comment operator # immediately with an opening bracket is not supported as a comment anymore since this syntax is now used for attributes.
reason: Real (parse error from 8.0, fixture), but the scanner cannot see it: the bundled php-parser has no reverse emulation for #[ (AttributeEmulator::reverseEmulate is a TODO), so such a file is rejected by both grammars and only shows up as 'could not be parsed'; a #[ that parses as an attribute on 8.0 is ordinary modern code.

quote: Inheritance errors due to incompatible method signatures (LSP violations) will now always generate a fatal error.
reason: Php80BicCoreIncompatibleOverride reports an override of a concrete parent method in the same file whose parameter list conflicts (more required, fewer, dropped variadic, by-reference): warning on 7.4, compile error from 8.0; types are not compared, and parents in other files (WP_Widget, Walker_Nav_Menu) are not judged.

quote: The precedence of the concatenation operator has changed relative to bitshifts and addition as well as subtraction.
reason: Php80BicCoreConcatPrecedence reports '.' followed by an unparenthesized +, -, << or >> (deprecated 7.4 at compile time, changed from 8.0); arithmetic before the '.' means the same on every version.

quote: Arguments with a default value that resolves to null at runtime will no longer implicitly mark the argument type as nullable.
reason: Depends on the value of the constant at run time (usually defined elsewhere); with a null value the call ran on 7.4 and is a TypeError from 8.0.

quote: A number of warnings have been converted into Error exceptions:
reason: Every listed case depends on run-time values (null or scalar variables, PHP_INT_MAX keys, array keys, unpacked strings); the five warnings are Errors from 8.0 on the runtimes. The notice-to-warning half changes no output and no claim can express it, so it has no fixture.

quote: Attempting to assign multiple bytes to a string offset will now emit a warning.
reason: Whether the target is a string and the value longer than one byte is a run-time matter; the runtimes show only a new warning from 8.0 and the same result, hence the empty claim.

quote: Unexpected characters in source files (such as null bytes outside of strings) will now result in a ParseError exception instead of a compile warning.
reason: Real (7.4 ran it, ParseError from 8.0, fixture), but the scanner's parser rejects such a file with both grammars, so it is only reported as 'could not be parsed'; stray NUL bytes are not plausible in plugin source.

quote: Uncaught exceptions now go through "clean shutdown", which means that destructors will be called after an uncaught exception.
reason: Destructors after an uncaught exception run after the fixture harness has written its report (the harness also catches every throwable itself), so no fixture can show the difference; whether an exception goes uncaught is a run-time matter.

quote: Compile time fatal error "Only variables can be passed by reference" has been delayed until runtime and converted to "Argument cannot be passed by reference" exception.
reason: Only moves an error from compile time to run time: code with such a call failed on 7.4 already, and code that ran on 7.4 is unaffected, so there is nothing to report.

quote: Some "Only variables should be passed by reference" notices have been converted to "Argument cannot be passed by reference" exception.
reason: The runtimes did not show any converted case: dynamic calls with a literal for a by-reference parameter were already an Error on 7.4, and end( explode() ) and call_user_func_array() with values stay a notice/warning on 8.5; without an observed case nothing is reported.

quote: The generated name for anonymous classes has changed.
reason: Only code that inspects the generated class name sees it, and that is a run-time string; class@anonymous on 7.4, ArrayObject@anonymous from 8.0.

quote: Non-absolute trait method references in trait alias adaptations are now required to be unambiguous:
reason: Php80BicCoreAmbiguousTraitAlias reports an alias without a trait name for a method that two used traits in the same file have; the runtimes show the 8.0 compile error even when insteadof settles the conflict and for visibility-only aliases.

quote: The signature of abstract methods defined in traits is now checked against the implementing class method:
reason: Php80BicCoreAbstractTraitMethod reports a class method that conflicts with a public/protected abstract trait method of the same file (parameter list, or different built-in scalar return types); 7.4 accepted it silently. The notes' own example (abstract private) is a compile error on 7.4 already.

quote: Disabled functions are now treated exactly like non-existent functions.
reason: disable_functions is an INI setting of the host, not something the source expresses.

quote: data: stream wrappers are no longer writable, which matches the documented behavior.
reason: Depends on the stream URL and mode at run time; fopen( 'data:...', 'w' ) fails on every version, while 'r+' wrote on 7.4 and fwrite() returns false from 8.0. Not plausible as literal code in plugins.

quote: The arithmetic and bitwise operators +, -, *, /, **, %, <<, >>, &, |, ^, ~, ++, -- will now consistently throw a TypeError when one of the operands is an array, resource or non-overloaded object.
reason: Operand types are run-time values; object + 1 was a notice on 7.4 and a TypeError from 8.0 (array + int was already fatal on 7.4).

quote: Float to string casting will now always behave locale-independently.
reason: Depends on the locale set at run time; the php-wasm runtimes accept setlocale( LC_ALL, 'de_DE.UTF-8' ) but print 1.5 on 7.4 too, so the change cannot be shown here and the fixture claim is empty.

quote: Removed support for deprecated curly braces for offset access
reason: Covered by the existing CurlyOffset rule.

quote: Applying the final modifier on a private method will now produce a warning unless that method is the constructor.
reason: Visible in the source, but on every runtime it is only a compile warning (seen through error_get_last(), as a user error handler never gets E_COMPILE_WARNING) with unchanged behaviour; the finding levels (deprecated, changed, error) have no level for a warning, so no rule reports it.

quote: If an object constructor exit()s, the object destructor will no longer be called.
reason: Whether a constructor reaches exit() is a run-time matter, and the destructor output on 7.4 comes after the fixture harness has written its report, so the runtimes cannot be shown the difference here.

quote: Non-strict comparisons between numbers and non-numeric strings now work by casting the number to string and comparing the strings.
reason: Depends on the values compared; 0 == 'not-a-number' is true on 7.4 and false from 8.0.

quote: Namespaced names can no longer contain whitespace: While `Foo\Bar` will be recognized as a namespaced name, `Foo \ Bar` will not.
reason: Real (parse error from 8.0, fixture), but the bundled php-parser reads names as single tokens with both grammars, so such a file is only reported as 'could not be parsed'; the new\x reinterpretation is not plausible in plugin code.

quote: Nested ternaries now require explicit parentheses.
reason: Covered by the existing NestedTernary rule.

quote: debug_backtrace() and Exception::getTrace() will no longer provide references to arguments.
reason: Only code that writes into debug_backtrace() args sees it, and which frame is written is a run-time value; with a by-reference parameter the write reached the variable on 7.4 and no longer from 8.0.

quote: Numeric string handling has been altered to be more intuitive and less error-prone.
reason: String contents are run-time values; is_numeric( '42 ' ) is false on 7.4 and true from 8.0, and 'many' * 2 was a warning on 7.4 and is a TypeError from 8.0. '5 apples' + 1 only went from notice to warning with the same result.

quote: Magic Methods will now have their arguments and return types checked if they have them declared.
reason: Php80BicCoreMagicMethodSignature reports declared magic method types 8.0 rejects at compile time (wrong return type of __isset/__set/__unset/__wakeup/__sleep/__serialize/__unserialize/__toString/__set_state, non-string name parameter); the runtimes also reject __toString(): int although the notes do not list __toString, and accept __set( $n, int $v ).

quote: call_user_func_array() array keys will now be interpreted as parameter names, instead of being silently ignored.
reason: Php80BicCoreCallUserFuncArrayKeys binds a literal argument array with string keys to a same-file function or closure on both versions: call.call_user_func_array_named_error when 8.0 throws (unknown name, positional after named), call.call_user_func_array_named_order when values reach other parameters (changed); arrays built at run time are not judged.
